ourfourcoreyugas.name: Satya Yuga
ourfourcoreyugas.subtitle: Dharma age
description: This is the first and most pure age where truth (satya) and righteousness (dharma) are at 100%
People are naturally good, honest, and follow moral values without being taught
There is no crime, no greed, and no suffering in society
Humans live very long lives (thousands of years) and have strong physical and mental health
People are deeply spiritual and have direct connection with the divine (God)
Meditation and inner realization are the main practices, not rituals
Nature is balanced and peaceful; no natural disasters or imbalance
Society does not need strict rules or laws because everyone follows dharma naturally

ourfourcoreyugas.name: Treta Yuga
ourfourcoreyugas.subtitle: Divine age
description: Dharma reduces slightly to about 75%, meaning some decline in truth and purity
People begin to develop ego, desires, and social hierarchy
This is the age of the great epic
Divine incarnations like Lord Rama appear to restore dharma
People still follow spiritual practices, but more structured rituals and sacrifices (yajnas) begin
Lifespans are still long but shorter than Satya Yuga
Society starts forming kingdoms, rules, and systems of governance
Good and evil both exist, but good is still dominant

ourfourcoreyugas.name: Dvapara Yuga
ourfourcoreyugas.subtitle: Dharma age
description: Dharma is reduced to 50%, meaning balance between good and bad
This is the age of the epic  and the teachings of Bhagavad Gita
Conflicts, wars, and complexity in life increase significantly
People become more materialistic and less spiritually aware
Temples, idol worship, and external rituals become more common
Human lifespan and strength decrease further
Knowledge is still present, but people struggle to follow it completely
Divine incarnations like Lord Krishna appear to guide humanity

ourfourcoreyugas.name: Kali Yuga
ourfourcoreyugas.subtitle: Folk age
description: This is the current age, where dharma is only 25% remaining
Materialism, ignorance, greed, and conflict dominate society
Truth is often ignored, and falsehood becomes common
People have shorter lifespans, weaker health, and more stress
Spiritual understanding is low, and distractions are very high
Following dharma becomes difficult, but still possible with effort
Simple practices like devotion (bhakti), chanting, and remembering God are most effective
Even though it is a dark age, liberation (moksha) is still possible for sincere seekers

home.ourfourcoreyugassubtitle: The eternal and universal way of life based on truth, righteousness, and spiritual principles that uphold cosmic order. These numbers are not random. They are derived from a base unit of 432,000, multiplied proportionally (4: 3: 2: 1). One Full Day of Brahma: Lifetime of Brahma - 100 Brahma years - Each year = 360 days - Each day = 4 yugas (ages) - Total = 311,040,000,000 human years.
home.scaling_comment: This mathematical scaling is highly structured and proportional across all cosmic levels.

sections.title: What is Sanatana Dharma?
sections.content: Sanatana Dharma means the 'eternal way of living.' It is not just a religion, but a way of understanding life, nature, and the universe. It teaches how to live in harmony with truth and cosmic order.
insights: Focuses on understanding reality rather than following fixed rules
Encourages questioning and personal experience of truth
Sees life as a journey of learning and inner growth
Teaches that happiness comes from alignment with truth, not external things
real_life_examples: Making decisions based on values, not pressure

sections.title: Sanatana Dharma Explained in Simple Terms
sections.content: Sanatana Dharma explains life using simple but powerful ideas that guide how we think, act, and grow.
insights: You are responsible for your life through your choices
Balance is important — not too materialistic, not too detached
Growth happens through experience, not just knowledge
Inner peace is more important than temporary pleasure
real_life_examples: Working honestly even when no one is watching
Learning from mistakes instead of blaming others

sections.title: 🌿 Core Principles of Sanatana Dharma
sections.content: These are the fundamental ideas that guide a meaningful and balanced life.
advanced_understanding: Dharma is not fixed — it changes based on situation and role
Karma is not punishment — it is a natural law of balance
Moksha is freedom from mental attachment, not just rebirth
Atman realization means understanding your true identity beyond body and mind
common_misunderstandings: Dharma is not religion — it is right action
Karma is not fate — actions can change outcomes
Moksha is not escaping life — it is understanding life fully

items.title: Dharma (Duty)
items.description: Living responsibly by doing what is right in every situation.
details: Guides your decisions in personal and social life
Changes based on your role (student, parent, leader)

items.title: Karma (Action)
items.description: Every action has a consequence, whether good or bad.
details: Negative actions lead to challenges or suffering

items.title: Moksha (Liberation)
items.description: Freedom from the cycle of birth and death.
details: Achieved through knowledge, devotion, and discipline
Brings permanent peace and unity with the divine

items.title: Ahimsa (Non-violence)
items.description: Avoid harming any living being in thought, word, or action.
details: Applies to humans, animals, and nature

sections.title: Main Scriptures of Sanatana Dharma
sections.content: These sacred texts preserve spiritual knowledge and guide people toward truth and right living.
insights: Different texts serve different purposes — rituals, philosophy, stories
They are meant to be understood, not blindly followed
Stories are symbolic and contain deeper meanings
Teachings can be applied differently based on time and context
how_to_use: Start with simple texts before deep philosophy
Focus on understanding meaning, not memorizing
Apply one teaching at a time in daily life

items.title: Vedas
items.description: The oldest sacred texts containing knowledge about nature, rituals, and truth.
details: Considered the foundation of Sanatana Dharma
Include hymns, prayers, and philosophical ideas
Explain cosmic laws and spiritual practices

items.title: Upanishads
items.description: Teachings about the soul (Atman) and ultimate reality (Brahman).

items.title: Puranas
items.description: Stories and teachings about gods, creation, and moral values.

items.title: Bhagavad Gita
items.description: A guide to life and duty through a conversation between Krishna and Arjuna.
details: Teaches how to handle life’s challenges

items.title: Ramayana & Mahabharata
items.description: Epic stories that teach values, duty, and righteousness.
details: Explain consequences of right and wrong actions

sections.title: Why Sanatana Dharma Matters Today
sections.content: Even in modern life, these teachings provide guidance for living peacefully and meaningfully.
modern_relevance: Helps manage stress and anxiety through acceptance
Provides ethical guidance in complex situations
practical_impact: Better relationships through understanding and patience

sections.title: Benefits of Following Sanatana Dharma
deeper_benefits: Creates long-term happiness instead of temporary pleasure

sections.title: Start Your Spiritual Journey
sections.content: Begin your journey step by step by learning, practicing, and experiencing.
step_by_step_path: Learn basic concepts like dharma and karma
Observe your thoughts and actions daily
beginner_tips: Do not try to learn everything at once
Focus on practice more than theory
Stay consistent even with small steps
